newsitem.title: GERMANY: Czech banker Tosovsky says sticks by prices goal.
newsitem.headline: Czech banker Tosovsky says sticks by prices goal.

text.p: Czech central bank governor Josef Tosovsky said on Monday that the central bank was sticking by its eight percent inflation target for 1997 despite planned price deregulations.
"We do expect some increases in price (when the planned price deregulations take effect) but we are not changing our plan, we are sticking by eight percent," Tosovsky told Reuters in an interview.
Tosovsky was in Frankfurt to present Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg with the European Banker of the Year award, which Tosovsky won for 1995.
The central bank was sticking to its inflation outlook even though the Czech finance ministry recently said inflation would likely rise after the deregulation plans were announced.
On Friday Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik revised upwards the government's 1997 inflation outlook to 9.5 percent after the ruling coalition parties moved to ease Communist-era price controls.
Average annual inflation was 8.8 percent last year and Tosovsky said the nation had recently enjoyed declining prices.
Government coalition partners last week agreed to increase rent prices on state-controlled housing and to raise value added tax on gas and electricity to 22 percent from five percent from July 1.
